key_gap: Both sides produced the identical forecast — mean 3,105 (median 3,105, trimmed 3,106), SD ≈ 216, 95% band 2,673–3,537 against a grader truth of 3,100 — and both ran the independence audit (ten structurally separate channels: dock counts, credit memos, carrier claims, inspection samples, ERP entries, supplier records; no shared feed, no draft-sharing). The gap is ordering and ownership: the human audits the precondition (structural independence) as the FIRST move and owns the signature lines — 'whoever's closest is luck, the average is structure' and the failure condition 'if they all read the same report, averaging is herding and the spread is a lie' — while the AI reaches the same answer by enumerating and verifying mean/median/trimmed variants inside HOW before selecting, stating the same insight later and more formally.
learning_signal: Averaging's power is entirely conditional on independence — the ensemble move is: (1) audit the sources BEFORE any arithmetic: enumerate each estimator's data channel and check for shared inputs, common reports, and draft-sharing — error cancellation requires independent noise, and the audit is the entire method; (2) compute the mean and report the spread (SD/range) — the average without the spread is a lie; (3) treat aggregation stability (mean ≈ median ≈ trimmed) as supporting evidence for independence, stated in one line; (4) do NOT trim endpoints without a cause — a structurally real channel is structure, and trimming is cherry-picking; (5) declare the calibration: a confidence band from the spread, plus the explicit failure condition (if sources share an input, the average is herding).
suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory 'independence audit' pre-pass at the WHAT/WHY boundary for every aggregation/forecast task: (a) WHAT must ask 'is averaging even allowed here?' before WHY models the aggregation; (b) WHY enumerates each source's data channel and emits an independence verdict (shared inputs, common reports, draft-sharing) before any mean is computed; (c) HOW defaults to the mean + spread as the first candidate and uses median/trimmed only as a stability confirmation, not as the opening move; (d) the decision packet must state the independence precondition and its failure condition ('correlated errors do not cancel') on every ensemble forecast.

key_gap: The pure style executed its core move and failed on it: it saw nine of ten estimates converging at ±2.8% (209–221M), treated the tight spread as confirmation, averaged to 211.8M (error 27.8M, +15% against the 184M actual), and its outlier-robustness reflex absorbed — or would have trimmed — the one correct signal (Analyst I's 186M, error 2M). It never checked the precondition: all nine 'diverse' estimates derived from one leaked IMS-backed draft with a discredited ramp assumption, and six analysts traded drafts. The AI ran the dependence audit FIRST — read the methodology provenance, found the single shared document and the draft-sharing group, diagnosed the tight spread as a correlation symptom — and forecast ≈186M with a wide 174–198M interval, declaring that averaging cannot cancel an error everyone shares.
learning_signal: The ensemble's failure mode is herding blindness: (1) before averaging ANY set of 'diverse' estimates, run the dependence audit — enumerate each estimator's named inputs and flag any single document, report, or draft that more than one cites; (2) treat a suspiciously tight spread as a correlation symptom, not a precision signal — independent estimates of an unannounced quantity do not converge to ±3%; the spread is a lie exactly when the herd looks most confident; (3) run the reverse-outlier test: if the outlier's channel is structurally independent of the herd's inputs, it is the signal, not noise — never trim it toward the consensus; (4) understand why the average fails here: error cancellation requires independent noise, so the mean of a herded crowd is one opinion in ten masks and inherits the shared error; (5) emit the averaging precondition ('independent channels') as an explicit verdict in the packet, not an assumption.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'dependence verdict' gate in the WHY stage for all aggregation/forecast tasks: (a) list every named input source per estimator and flag duplicate citations/shared documents/draft-sharing groups before any mean is computed; (b) flag tight spreads (within ~5%) as requiring an independence explanation before confidence is granted — a tight spread without audited independence is a red flag, not a signal; (c) mandate the reverse-outlier test: for any outlier, decide independent-channel vs noise BEFORE any trimming decision, with the structurally independent outlier treated as the strongest signal in the set; (d) the decision packet must state whether error cancellation applies, and if not, forecast from the independent channel with a widened interval and declare the rejection of the herd mean with its shared-error reason.
